title: Solar Lead Generation: A Guide for Installers
html:
Solar lead generation is how an installer gets homeowners to request a quote. It runs through own marketing, such as Google Ads, SEO and Meta ads, or through bought solar leads.

To generate solar leads, set a cost ceiling, run Google Ads, build solar SEO pages and call every lead within minutes. This guide is for solar installers deciding between their own marketing and bought leads.

You need a quote form, a phone that is answered, and a budget you can hold for 90 days. Free steps cost time, and paid steps cost an ad budget that you pay to Google or Meta directly.

What you need first

You need a ceiling price per lead, a tracking sheet, a landing page and a person who calls leads fast. These four items keep your spend tied to signed installs.

Should you buy solar leads or generate your own?

Generate your own leads when you can hold a 90-day budget and track results. Buy leads when you need volume this month and the price fits your ceiling. Many installers use both and compare the cost per signed install.

Factor Own marketing Bought solar leads
Who else gets the lead Only you Often several installers
Speed to first lead Slower to build Fast
Control over message High Low
Cost pattern Ad budget plus management Fee per lead
Best for A steady pipeline Filling a gap

Use this rule for any lead price. The most you should pay is your close rate times gross profit per install, halved to leave profit.

Sample math with made-up numbers: if a bought lead closes at 5% and an install leaves $4,000 in gross profit, the cap is $100. If your own exclusive lead closes at 10%, the cap is $200. Use your own numbers.

Steps for solar lead generation

These 7 steps run from the foundation to the paid channels. Do steps 1 and 2 before you spend on ads.

1. Set your cost ceiling and tracking

Work out the most you can pay per lead and per signed install. Every later choice depends on these two numbers.

  • Divide signed installs by leads to get your close rate for each source.
  • Multiply by gross profit per install and halve the result.
  • Log source, call time and result in one sheet.

Checkpoint: each lead source has its own ceiling. Work it out from that source's close rate and your profit per install.

Mistake to avoid: comparing sources by cost per lead alone, instead of cost per signed install.

2. Build a solar landing page that earns the quote

Use one landing page with one offer and one form. A page built for one action keeps the visitor focused, unlike a home page with ten links.

  • Lead with the homeowner's goal: a lower power bill and a clear quote.
  • Explain financing offers in plain words and link no more than one.
  • Add a short form and a click-to-call button above the fold.

Checkpoint: the page loads fast on a phone. Mistake to avoid: asking for ten fields before a quote.

3. Run Google Ads on solar quote searches

Bid on searches that show buying intent, such as solar installers near me and solar panel cost. Paid search reaches homeowners who are ready to ask for a quote.

  • Target your real service area and your licensed states only.
  • Group ads by intent: cost, install, financing and local installer.
  • Send each ad group to a matching landing page.

Checkpoint: cost per lead stays under your ceiling after the learning period.

Mistake to avoid: bidding on broad terms like solar, which brings in students and researchers.

4. Build solar SEO pages for local intent

Write one page per service and per city you serve. Organic pages bring in leads at no click cost after they rank.

  • Create pages for residential solar, battery storage and commercial solar.
  • Add a page for each main city or county you install in.
  • Keep your business profile and reviews current with local SEO.

Checkpoint: each page answers cost, process and timeline questions.

Mistake to avoid: copying manufacturer text that every installer already uses.

5. Use Meta ads for awareness and retargeting

Run Facebook and Instagram ads to reach homeowners before they search. Meta works best with a simple offer such as a free savings estimate.

  • Use one real install photo and one clear offer.
  • Target homeowners in your service area.
  • Retarget visitors who left the quote form unfinished.

Checkpoint: track cost per lead and appointment rate separately. Meta ads management is $1,999 a month plus ad spend; see Meta ads for solar.

Mistake to avoid: judging Meta by quote forms alone, since many leads need a call to qualify.

Get the free contractor marketing guide

  • Ask each vendor whether the lead is shared and with how many installers.
  • Run a 30-day test with a fixed lead count.
  • Compare cost per signed install with your own Google Ads.

Checkpoint: stop any vendor that stays above your ceiling. Mistake to avoid: signing a long contract before the 30-day test finishes.

7. Follow up in minutes and qualify on the first call

Call every lead as soon as it arrives and ask four questions. Speed matters because homeowners may request quotes from several installers.

  • Call within minutes, then text if there is no answer.
  • Ask about the roof, the power bill, the home owner and the timeline.
  • Book the appointment before you end the call.

Checkpoint: every lead has a call time logged. Mistake to avoid: sending a quote by email with no call.

How do you know solar lead generation is working?

Solar lead generation is working when cost per signed install stays under your ceiling and call speed stays fast. Review five numbers monthly and change one thing at a time.

Maximum price per lead = close rate x gross profit per install, halved. Check it for every lead source each month.

Common solar lead problems and fixes

Most solar lead problems trace back to slow calls, weak landing pages or shared leads. Each one has a quick fix.

Problem Likely cause Fix
Leads do not answer Another installer called first Call within minutes and text right after
Quotes do not close Weak first-call qualifying Ask about roof, bill, ownership and timeline
Cost per lead is high Broad keywords or a wide area Narrow to your service area and buying terms
Bought leads are duplicates Shared lead sold to many Ask for exclusivity in writing or drop the vendor
Ads get clicks but few forms Weak landing page Use one offer, one form and click-to-call

Pay for a solar lead only when your close rate says it can pay you back.

How do you generate solar leads?

Generate solar leads by running Google Ads on quote searches and building local solar SEO pages. Add Meta ads for reach and call every lead within minutes. Send each source to a dedicated landing page and track cost per signed install. Buy leads only when the price fits your cost ceiling.

How much do solar leads cost?

Solar lead prices vary by state, whether the lead is shared or exclusive, and how well it is qualified. Instead of trusting an average, set your ceiling: close rate times gross profit per install, halved. Paid search clicks for solar lead terms run about $10 to $16 each, according to Ahrefs.

Are exclusive solar leads worth it?

Exclusive solar leads can be worth it because only you call the homeowner, which raises your close rate. They cost more, so test a fixed number for 30 days. Keep the vendor only if cost per signed install stays under your ceiling.

What are the best solar lead generation companies?

The best solar lead generation company is the one that keeps your cost per signed install under your ceiling. Ask each vendor if leads are shared, how they are qualified and what the refund policy is. Test before you sign, and compare vendors with your own Google Ads results.

Final advice

Set your cost ceiling first, then pick one paid channel and one organic channel to test for 90 days. If you want help, a home services marketing agency can build the landing pages, run the ads and track every lead to a signed install.
